newsitem.title: ARGENTINA: Argentine bonds end up, more gains seen possible.
newsitem.headline: Argentine bonds end up, more gains seen possible.

text.p: Argentine bonds finished higher Friday as uplifting news of a balanced budget accord in the U.S. boosted prices and many traders predicted further gains next week.
"Investors are positive and the market is fundamentally firm," said a trader.
Argentina's FRB Brady bond due 2005 was up 1/4 at 92-1/2, while the dollar-denominated Bocon Previsional 4 due 2002 rose $0.85 to 115.10.
"My short-term outlook is positive, but I would beware of possible profit-taking," said Roberto Costa Bourdieu, senior fixed income analyst at Banco Rio, pointing to the strong gains over this week.
With the moderate U.S. indicators released this week, traders have taken heart that the Federal Reserve may not hike rates as aggressively as some feared a few weeks ago.
The biggest event on the domestic scene next week, said traders, will be the auction Tuesday of $500 million of Bonte Treasury bonds.
Call money rates rose to 5.53 percent from 5.48 percent.
